reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 33. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 2. Of 38 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 38 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 211 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text:
The courage and sacrifice of the USS Indianapolis crew deserve lasting recognition.

I support @SenatorBanks request for the Navy to review awarding the ship that carried the name of our capital city in WWII — and its crew — with a Battle Star for their final combat engagement.

Their service remains a proud part of our city’s history.
https://t.co/VeLqraPsAv

Good news for Richmond: Our Eastern IN community ranked 9th for affordability among 260 urban areas in the latest quarterly cost-of-living survey.

That matters to families making a household budget, and employers looking for a place to grow. Wayne County has a strong story to

Indiana leads the nation in Japanese investment per capita, with Japanese businesses supporting 62,000 Hoosier jobs.

I joined @RepJillTokuda as we were welcomed as the new bipartisan House Co-Chairs of the Congressional Study Group on Japan.

From Subaru’s arrival in Indiana in 1986 to today, our partnership with Japan has grown to support manufacturing, innovation and good-paying jobs across our state.

I look forward to strengthening our economic and security ties with one of America’s closest allies.

Honor Flight brings veterans from across America to Washington free of charge, to visit the memorials built in their honor.

I joined Hoosier veterans at the National Museum of American History for A Tribute to American Veterans. It was a privilege to hear their stories and thank https://t.co/t6jHajWgaZ

Our combat-wounded veterans should receive the full military retirement pay they’ve earned, alongside the VA disability benefits they deserve.

Today, I voted YES on the Major Richard Star Act, legislation I cosponsored to end this unfair reduction in benefits for tens of thousands of veterans, including Hoosiers.

They’ve earned both through service and sacrifice. It’s overdue.

On Veterans Day, we honor the Hoosiers and Americans who have served our nation in uniform. Their courage and sacrifice protect the freedoms we hold dear.

To all our veterans, today and every day, thank you for your service. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/k2mZuzWndy

Sports help drive central Indiana’s economy. When fans come to town, they fill hotel rooms, eat at our  restaurants, and support Hoosier jobs.

Thanks to @IndSportsCorp for bringing us together in Indianapolis for our annual State of Sports celebration. https://t.co/ZUF9ZNOM5k

It’s an honor to continue representing Indiana’s Sixth District in Congress. I work for everyone who calls this district home.

My team and I will keep working with Hoosiers across all 11 counties of #IN06 and making sure your voice is heard in Washington. 

Hoosiers have always been my first priority, and they always will be. 🇺🇸

Election Day is tomorrow, November 3.

Our right to vote carries a responsibility to use it. 

If you haven’t already voted, make your voice heard. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/C6c6WDqQZS

Here at home this October, I hosted Hoosiers in Columbus for our Stop Scams Summit and talked with AP Government students at Shelbyville High School.

Thanks to everyone who has stopped to talk. I always appreciate hearing what’s on your mind.

Catch up on my work across the Sixth District in the latest Shreve Summary: https://t.co/p4iEJf9RRN
Happy Halloween from the Shreves! 🎃 https://t.co/QAFQjIdLJH

It was good to be back in the Indianapolis City-County Council chamber, where I once served, for the annual Public Servants’ Prayer service.

That room holds a lot of memories. It’s where I learned firsthand the responsibilities of local government and the importance of seeking wisdom beyond our own.

Thanks to Pastor Tim Lindsey and Public Servants’ Prayer for bringing us together in faith and reminding us of the importance of humility and service. #IN06

In Lynn, keeping the community safe means looking out for your neighbors. I visited with the town marshal and a Randolph County school resource officer to hear about their work serving local families.

We remember Town Marshal Brad Fisher, who lost his life in the line of duty. https://t.co/VKaxpztUl9

@SAICinc’s Indianapolis team designs, builds, and repairs equipment that keeps our military aircraft ready to fly. Nearly 100 of the company’s employees call Indiana’s Sixth District home.

I toured their plant this week to see the work firsthand. Thanks to the SAIC team for the https://t.co/ysTwM5d2T9

Serving Hoosiers starts with showing up, listening, and helping solve problems. That’s why my team and I bring our office to you.

Over the past year, we’ve held 33 mobile office hours across all 11 counties of Indiana’s 6th District, helping Hoosiers with things like VA claims, https://t.co/xNLQ6BRTRH

Learning how our government works is part of learning how to shape it.

I visited Shelbyville High School’s AP U.S. Government and Politics students to discuss my work in Congress, how bills become law, and the responsibility of representing our Sixth District.

Thanks to Principal Amy Dawson and teacher Vince Bradburn for welcoming me into the classroom.

Hoosier manufacturers compete around the world. The cost of importing parts can make that harder.

I represent Indianapolis International Airport, right here in Indiana’s Sixth District. Its Foreign-Trade Zone program helps businesses manage those costs and reach customers overseas.

I met with Executive Director Mario Rodriguez and his team to identify ways Congress can support that work and strengthen Indiana manufacturing. #IN06

The best part of this job is spending time with the Hoosiers I represent and hearing what matters in our communities.

This week, I met with local leaders, helped break ground on a new terminal at Richmond Municipal Airport, and visited with Hoosiers across the Sixth District. https://t.co/DweXc0qQXv

Today is the last day to apply for FEMA Individual Assistance after the August storms and flooding.

If you had damage or losses, there's still time. Apply at https://t.co/NtZ0rIkC4C or through the FEMA app.

https://t.co/NzR6GQcCag

For 110 years, the Indiana Masonic Home in Franklin has endured because each generation took responsibility for the next. Its history includes giving 814 children a place to belong. 

Today, it helps seniors live with dignity and the care they need. 

I joined residents, staff, Masons, and the Order of the Eastern Star to celebrate that legacy this week. Thanks to everyone who keeps that promise going.

This Sunday, October 25, is the deadline to apply for FEMA assistance after August’s storms and flooding.

Hoosiers in eligible counties can apply at https://t.co/UkBnVhasHY or call 1-800-621-3362.

Need help? Call my office at (317) 399-3333. 

#IN06 https://t.co/Uv2sE8wf7m

100 Hoosiers joined us in Columbus today for our second STOP SCAMS Summit.

Thanks to local law enforcement, community bankers, the FBI, and state agency experts for helping Hoosiers recognize fraud and protect their hard-earned money.

The best way to stop a scam is to spot it https://t.co/b5ou4wMz6S

Scammers count on catching you off guard. 

Join me this afternoon in Columbus for our second STOP SCAMS Summit to learn how to spot fraud and protect your money.

Hear from local law enforcement, community bankers, and experts from the FBI and state agencies. All are welcome.

It takes too long and costs too much to build a house these days.

I introduced the Build More Homes Act to help communities cut red tape and make homebuilding faster and less expensive.

The idea is simple: Study how pre-approved home designs can reduce permitting delays and https://t.co/vsnY08uP0p

Harvest is in full swing at Ramsey Farms in Shelby County.

Phil Ramsey let me take the wheel of a combine at his family’s sixth-generation farm, where they grow corn, soybeans, wheat, and sunflowers and produce seed for @BecksHybrids.

I appreciate Phil and his sons making time https://t.co/2cGNtYLtBO

Federal funding doesn’t begin with a check from Washington. It begins with local communities doing the groundwork.

That was our focus in Shelby County as we looked ahead to 2027 Community Project Funding.

If your town has a project on the drawing board —now’s the time to talk https://t.co/Q4ukAnxFqI

At @HoopsHall in New Castle, I met with Hoosiers to discuss 2027 funding for roads, water and sewer upgrades, and first responder equipment.

I’ve advanced $56 million for 6th District projects this Congress. 

Our communities set the priorities. My job is to help secure the https://t.co/RErM0yDnft

Caring for our neighbors takes skill, patience, and compassion.

Last week, I visited Envive Healthcare in Beech Grove, formerly St. Paul Hermitage, to hear from the team providing nursing care and rehabilitation for Hoosiers.

Thanks to Ben Wells for the tour and to the nursing https://t.co/XuKAjiuLqk

Strong schools and a strong local economy go hand in hand.

In the Columbus area, the Community Education Coalition brings educators and employers together to connect education and training with the skills our businesses need.

I met with Dr. Jim Roberts and Ashley Dieter to https://t.co/lftdAoWwT3

Got an idea for an app? Let’s see what our students can build.

The Congressional App Challenge is open to middle and high school students who live or attend school in the Sixth District. Enter on your own or with a team, using any coding language.

Register by October 26. Visit https://t.co/QxJuEMtXaa

Scott Allman of Zeller Insurance in Columbus stopped by our Bartholomew County office hours to discuss legislation affecting the insurance industry.

Hearing directly from local professionals helps me understand how decisions in Washington affect our businesses and the Hoosiers https://t.co/D3uUIRxDNl

That “local” Indiana number calling you may not be local at all.

SIM boxes route overseas calls through hundreds of SIM cards, making scammers look like neighbors. 

Today I introduced the Stop SIM Box Scams Act to ban these devices and help federal agencies keep them out of our https://t.co/58NkSdqzWZ
https://t.co/AnQxtThtgP

Our neighbors in Connersville, Cambridge City and New Castle face a long recovery from last month’s floods. I’ve visited these communities, and my team and I are staying engaged as they rebuild.

My September newsletter covers those visits, the October 25 deadline to apply for

Indy Southsiders, we're bringing the office to you.

Our constituent services team will be at the West Perry Library on Thursday afternoon. Bring your VA benefits, Social Security, IRS, passport, or FEMA and flood assistance questions. We'd be happy help you with them.

Walk-ins https://t.co/O1Q1REquAc

I’m reflecting this weekend on my visit last week in Washington with Archbishop Charles Thompson of the @archindy.

We discussed Pope Leo’s encyclical on artificial intelligence. I share his concern that technological progress must protect human dignity.

AI holds great promise — https://t.co/DzJGs35W77

Columbus, we are coming to you.

Our constituent services team will be at City Hall on Wednesday, September 30. VA benefits, Social Security, the IRS, passports, FEMA and flood assistance claims, or any other federal issue you need a hand with.

Stop by if you need a hand! #IN06 https://t.co/MQmKPRmRFs

Dr. Jeff Wargo of Richmond and fellow Indiana dermatologists came by my DC office to talk about the care they provide our communities. He treats many of our Wayne County veterans, including some I met with recently.

Their work detecting and treating skin cancer saves lives. https://t.co/L0a12Pjs4L

I get to work with mayors across our district as partners to advance local infrastructure needs.

Mayor Steve Barnett of Franklin and Mayor Mark Myers of Greenwood came by my DC office to talk Johnson County priorities. I advanced $1.1 million through the Appropriations Committee https://t.co/h3fNzDpS4z

We broke ground on a new terminal at Richmond Municipal Airport. The current one is 80 years old. Wayne County needs a new gateway.

The city did the work to get this project ready. I advocated for the $1.4 million FAA award to help make it happen. With 15,000 operations a year, https://t.co/eihNzUkN0V

Thank you to Public Servants’ Prayer for visiting our Capitol office — and for the personalized Bible bearing our Indiana state seal.

I’m grateful for their prayers for me, my colleagues, and our country. We need wisdom and humility in this work! #IN06 https://t.co/F9nUeKA8iM

Indiana makes things that matter.
 At @AdvaMedUpdate Medtech Showcase, I joined @CookMedical and medical device companies from Greenwood and Franklin (along with their mayors) to see their work firsthand.

Local medical device manufacturers are helping improve patient care https://t.co/EQKHh6X39O

Thank you to Greenwood’s Andrea Bauer and the @ACSCAN volunteers for our conversation about cancer research funding and access to clinical trials.

For Hoosiers facing cancer, where you live shouldn’t limit your treatment options. I’m working to bring care closer to home. #IN06 https://t.co/drnaMrcimI

Senior Japanese lawmakers visited my office and the Capitol recently. No state draws more Japanese investment per person than Indiana. 

Japanese companies employ 70,000 Hoosiers. It’s a partnership we’re working to keep strong. #IN06 #JapanUS https://t.co/O42DtmBt8w

Mary and I joined Southside friends Friday night to celebrate Mental Health America of Indiana’s 75th anniversary.

We’re grateful for 75 years of speaking up for Hoosiers facing mental health challenges and their families. That work matters, and so do the people who keep it https://t.co/yt1XAJAMtv

Hoosier business leaders came to Washington this week to meet with Indiana’s congressional delegation. 

We talked about energy, workforce needs, and the regulations that can make it easier—or harder—to build and grow in Indiana.

Thank you to @IndianaChamber for bringing us https://t.co/uoDjwgcdI8

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
